newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares close mostly weaker in nervous mkt.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares close mostly weaker in nervous mkt.

text.p: Italian shares closed mostly weaker on Friday in a nervous market with gains by state telecoms group Stet balanced by continued declines by Telecom Italia while among banks Credito Italiano continued to walk tall.

Stet, which is due to merge with Telecom later this year, finished 1.34 percent higher at 8,446 lire while Telecom Italia drifted 0.46 percent lower to 4,543 lire. Investors are now expecting a higher share swap ratio than had originally been expected when the merger was first announced.
The all-share mibtel index finished 0.58 percent down at 12,514 while the blue chip mib30 index ended 0.78 percent lower at 18,639.
Brokers said domestic funds were active in the market, selectively unloading stock but also on the lookout for opportunities.
Food producer Parmalat was among the gainers, putting on 1.35 percent to close at 2,486 lire, as investors bought up the stock after rumours of a capital increase receded.
Energy group ENI and auto group Fiat, traditionally weather vanes of market sentiment, both finished the session above the day's lows, closing at 9,004 lire and 5,279 lire, respectively.
BCI finished 0.32 percent higher at 3,447 lire and Credito ended 1.63 percent higher at 2,366 lire.

Brokers said doubts about whether the government will be able to pass the 1998 budget early were also weighing on market sentiment. Earlier Prime Minister Romano Prodi said he would still like to bring forward the full 1998 budget but would need clear backing in parliament to do so.
